rows.estimation_basis: Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project #004 (Patient Appointment and Telehealth App, 3,900 hours, 22 weeks). We reused matching effort benchmarks for the Flutter mobile client (800-920h vs 900h ref), appointment scheduling engine (460-540h vs 520h ref), Twilio video integration (340-400h vs 380h ref), secure messaging & reminder systems (380-440h vs 420h ref), counsellor web dashboard (500-580h vs 560h ref), HIPAA security & audit logging (280-340h vs 300h ref), and QA / App Store submissions (320-380h vs 340h ref). Because the current brief does not require enterprise EHR / HL7 FHIR integration (which took 480h in the reference project), that scope was omitted, resulting in an adjusted baseline of approximately 3,280 to 3,860 engineering hours over a 20-week timeline.

Estimates are directly derived from reference project 007-edtech-lms (corporate training LMS delivered in 2,800 hours over 18 weeks with Angular, Django, PostgreSQL, and SCORM support). We retained comparable effort allocations for SCORM package parsing, quiz rules engines, video delivery, and certification tracking. Adjustments were applied to align with industrial workforce requirements, specifically emphasizing supervisor team hierarchies and automated compliance exports while maintaining rigorous QA and DevOps allocations.

Estimates are directly grounded in historical data from Reference Project 008-mobile-field-service (Offline-First Field Service App for Technicians, 3,600 total hours, 21 weeks). Module scopes map directly to reference historical benchmarks: offline data layer and sync engine (~760h baseline), job lists and inspection checklists (~520h baseline), photo/signature capture and upload queues (~300h baseline), dispatch/scheduling console (~640h baseline), ERP integration (~520h baseline), push notifications and background sync (~200h baseline), DevOps and release deployment (~260h baseline), and field testing/QA (~400h baseline). Historical lessons learned regarding conflict resolution complexity and mobile device fragmentation testing have been explicitly incorporated into the allocation matrix.

Estimates are directly grounded in historical data from Reference Project 001-logistics-fleet-portal (3,000 total hours, 20 weeks). Scoping adjustments were made to reflect the Eval Client project parameters: Telematics Integration was adjusted from 520h (3 vendors) down to 380-460h (2 vendors); Live Map was adjusted from 420h to 360-440h; Deviation & Alert Engine was calibrated around 340-420h; Vehicle/Driver CRUD reflects 200-260h; and Reporting was sized at 300-380h for daily route PDFs/CSVs. QA and DevOps allocations mirror the proportion observed in the reference project to ensure production-grade stability under peak operational loads.

No historical reference projects were provided for this brief. Estimates have been formulated bottom-up using industry-standard engineering benchmarks for real-time transactional auction platforms. Effort allocations explicitly incorporate architectural discovery, automated testing, DevOps provisioning, load testing for concurrency, and client UAT cycles.

No historical reference projects were provided in the RFP. Consequently, this estimate has been derived bottom-up based on standard enterprise engineering delivery baselines across discovery, architecture, UI/UX, full-stack implementation, testing, and deployment. The scope factors in significant non-functional effort including third-party API reliability handling (IDV and background checks), distributed locking for marketplace concurrency, financial ledger integrity for batch payouts, and dedicated compliance console tooling. Total team velocity assumes a multi-disciplinary squad comprising a Solutions Architect, two Full-Stack Engineers, a QA Automation Engineer, and a DevOps/Security Specialist operating over 20 delivery weeks.

Estimates are directly grounded in historical data from Reference Project 006-saas-analytics-dashboard (4,600 hours, 24 weeks, Angular/Python/ClickHouse/Kafka). The core customer-facing configurable dashboards, high-volume ClickHouse/Kafka time-series processing, and scheduled PDF reporting modules borrow their structure and sizing directly from this benchmark. Adjustments were made to incorporate scope additions unique to this brief: specifically, the installer-specific hardware provisioning portal (+480 hours net), dedicated IoT device registration and heartbeat workflows, and stream-based threshold notification rules (+460 hours net). QA, integration, DevOps, and multi-tenant security allocations reflect real-world delivery ratios derived from the historical project.

No historical reference projects were provided for this brief. The estimate was derived using a rigorous bottom-up work breakdown structure (WBS) reflecting enterprise pharmaceutical standards. Effort incorporates end-to-end delivery including regulatory compliance audits, offline sync conflict architecture, mobile application engineering, AI citation engineering, automated QA, and Salesforce OAuth integration. Engineering uncertainty has been factored into the range distributions across complex offline and CRM integration modules.

No reference projects were provided; therefore, this estimate is derived bottom-up based on industry benchmarks and delivery team composition across discovery, architecture, mobile/web development, testing, and cloud operations. A conservative uncertainty factor has been incorporated into native mobile health API integrations, real-time video handling, and enterprise privacy safeguards.

Estimates are derived from historical data from Reference 001 (Fleet Tracking Portal) and Reference 008 (Offline-First Field Service App). The ERP integration (440-540h) is grounded in Reference 008's ERP integration (520h). The handheld scanning interface and local buffering (460-560h) adapt Reference 008's job forms and checklists (520h) adjusted for warehouse barcode input rather than field forms. Master data and auth reuse Reference 001's CRUD (240h) and Auth (160h). The discrepancy and replenishment engines (total 600-760h) replace Reference 001's alerting engine (380h) and KPI dashboards (360h). QA and DevOps reflect the combined learnings of both references, factoring in dedicated on-device handheld hardware validation.

The estimate is based on general industry experience and bottom-up engineering decomposition only, as no historical reference projects were provided. Effort ranges reflect a complete, production-ready human delivery lifecycle including discovery, full-stack development, mobile offline data synchronization, comprehensive multi-device QA, cloud DevOps, and store submission stabilization.

The estimate has been constructed bottom-up based on standard engineering benchmarks for custom workforce management applications, constraint satisfaction pipelines, cross-device web interfaces, rigorous automated testing, and release management. Hours account for full lifecycle delivery including discovery, backend constraint logic, frontend responsive calendar interactions, end-to-end QA, and post-launch operational stabilization.

No historical reference projects were provided. Estimates were derived bottom-up based on standard enterprise engineering standards, accounting for end-to-end SDLC phases including architecture, third-party API integration, automated testing, DevOps, security hardening, and hypercare.

No historical reference projects were provided for this brief. The estimate has been constructed strictly bottom-up based on standard production-grade enterprise delivery metrics. Hours reflect comprehensive full lifecycle delivery—including architectural design, CRDT sync engineering, granular classroom permission controls, cross-platform tablet touch testing, WebSocket load simulation, infrastructure setup, and automated CI/CD pipelines. Uncertainty has been accommodated through an approximate 30% variance between minimum and maximum bounds.
